question: Should outbound recovery keep ambiguous entries pending with backoff when no reconciliation-capable adapter is available, instead of moving them to failed after the current recovery pass?
rationale: Both states are defensible: pending preserves future recoverability, while terminal failed gives operators a clearer fail-closed state and avoids long-lived pending rows. Tests can prove either behavior, but they cannot choose the operator-facing product policy.

options.title: Accept Recoverable Pending
options.body: After the pacing defect is fixed and checks are green, merge the PR's pending/backoff behavior and keep full delivery-state surfacing under the broader canonical issue.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed State
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep current main's terminal failed behavior until a complete operator-facing delivery ledger is designed.

options.title: Require Operator Surface First
options.body: Ask for a doctor, UI, or Gateway/API surface before making ambiguous no-reconciler rows remain pending longer.

recommendation.title: Accept Recoverable Pending
recommendation.body: After the pacing defect is fixed and checks are green, merge the PR's pending/backoff behavior and keep full delivery-state surfacing under the broader canonical issue.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses core queue semantics, delivery recovery, and operator behavior, and this owner has the strongest recent history on the affected recovery path.
